title: fix(plugin-approvals)!: under a walled tenancy posture, an approval request with no organization is acted on only by a platform administrator or the system
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — the change is who the approval doors admit at runtime on a stored request with no organization; no published skill teaches the administrator override on such a request

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:在 `group` / `isolated` 墙内姿态下,没有组织归属的审批请求只放行平台管理员或系统;组织管理员在每个审批动作上得到与"请求不存在"相同的 `404 REQUEST_NOT_FOUND`,请求不变。没有活动组织的组织管理员会话在墙内也不再是列表、数据门可见性与待审记录读取上的越权持有者。
- 为什么改:ADR-0131 D1 规定 NULL 不是归属;按维护者裁决,组织管理员的权限止于本组织,`single` 姿态不变。
- 风险与回滚:只影响墙内姿态下 ADR-0131 D9 之前存下的无组织请求。这类请求在墙内本来就无法在门上被决定(D9 拒绝其动作记录的写入),补救是自愿的 `os migrate organization-ownership` 仪式。回滚 = 还原 `approval-service.ts` 中 `isOverrideActor` 的一行判断。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`(`isOverrideActor` 中 `requestOrg == null` 一行与新增 `organizationWallStands`);`approval-tenant-positions-name-authority.test.ts` 新增的顶层 describe;changeset。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/approval-tenant-positions-name-authority.test.ts`,预期 96 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

The rule (ADR-0131 D1: NULL is not a state and names no owner), applied where every approval door asks who may override:

- Under a walled tenancy posture (`group`, `isolated`), only a platform administrator or a system context is admitted to act on an approval request that carries no organization. Such a request is still not decided at the door: the action row a decision writes would carry no organization, which ADR-0131 D9 refuses at the engine, so nothing is written; the organization-ownership ceremony is the remedy. An organization administrator is answered on approve, reject, recall, reassign, revise (send back), resubmit, remind, request info and comment exactly as for an id that names no request (`REQUEST_NOT_FOUND`, `404` at the HTTP door), and the request is unchanged.
- Under `single`, nothing changes: a tenant administrator acts on such a request.
- A request that carries an organization keeps its rule: an administrator of that organization, or a platform administrator.
- The same rule holds where the organization asked is the caller's own: under a walled posture, a tenant administrator whose session carries no active organization is no override holder for the approvals list, the request visibility the data door reads, or the pending-approver record read.

`ApprovalService.isOverrideActor` is the one predicate every act door, the list door, its viewer flag, the data door's request visibility and the pending-approver read grant ask, so the rule is stated once there. The posture is read through the service's existing tenancy-posture provider and the shared spec predicate `postureEnforcesWall` (`organizationWallStands`, no second spelling). A stack with no tenancy service has no wall anywhere, so an absent posture reads as unwalled, the reading `vetOrganizationClaim` takes for an absent posture; an unrecognised value reads as absent too.

No backfill, no boot-time step, no change to `backfill-platform-row-organizations.ts` or the CLI inventory. The changeset points operators at the existing, voluntary `os migrate organization-ownership` ceremony (plan first, then `--apply`).

## Tests

- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-tenant-positions-name-authority.test.ts`: one new top-level describe in the shared harness for the tenant arm, with the tenant administrator resolved through the real `resolveUserAuthzGrants`.
  - Under `isolated` and under `group`, for each of the nine act doors: the tenant administrator is refused with the answer an id that names no request gets, and the request and its action history are unchanged; side by side, the refusal on the row and on a missing id are identical once the id is written out, and the read door answers both `null`.
  - The list door does not show the request to the tenant administrator; a system read lists it.
  - A hand-built tenant-administrator context with no active organization, under both walled postures: the data door's request visibility is the participant set without the request, the approvals list does not show it, and the pending-approver read grant does not reach its record; under `single` (CONTROL) the visibility is unrestricted, the list shows it and the grant reaches it.
  - CONTROLS, each on approve, reject, recall and reassign: a platform administrator and a system context are admitted and the write lands, under both walled postures; an organization's own administrator acts on that organization's request; an administrator of another organization is refused on an organization's request; under `single` the tenant administrator acts on a request with no organization.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-act-doors-read-visibility.dogfood.test.ts`: one new door-level case on a real `isolated` boot. The request's tenant column is first relaxed to the pre-18 shape with `relaxTenantColumns` (the three approval tables), and the row with no organization is planted below the engine. The owner of organization A and the owner of organization B each get, on every act door, the status and body an id that names no request gets, and nothing is written. CONTROL: the seeded platform administrator is not answered as unseen; the decision's action write is refused by ADR-0131 D9 (`500 APPROVAL_APPROVE_FAILED`, naming `sys_approval_action`), and nothing is written. CONTROL: A's owner decides A's own request.
- One-shot ablation of the new posture check, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, at 350bc40b6e (the guard line is unchanged since): 36 of 90 pins red, then restored (blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). The controls stayed green under the ablation, as they should.

## Acceptance notes

- At the HTTP door the approvals route relays the engine's D9 refusal under its own fault code `APPROVAL_APPROVE_FAILED` (500), not the engine's `ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`; unchanged here, noted only.
- An admitted caller whose active organization is not the request's (a platform administrator, or a tenant administrator under `single`, acting on a request with no organization) can be answered `READ_BACK_FAILED` after the write lands: the echo is read in the caller's organization scope. That is the existing, loud write-recorded answer and is unchanged here; the control pins accept it and assert the write landed.
- Not merged with `origin/main`: the commits since the base touch neither `plugin-approvals`, the dogfood file, nor the posture predicate.
- The provenance in the code comment is ADR-0131 D1; the maintainer's ruling is not linked from public text.
